title: Krishna upgrade proposal response (v1)
description: Normalized, versioned response shape a provider run (Codex or Claude Code) must produce for a read-only proposal or an implementation-review pass. A response that fails to validate against this schema is a failed run (error = "invalid_proposal_schema"), not a best-effort partial proposal. See docs/upgrades/ARCHITECTURE.md.

schemaVersion.description: Must match this schema file's version exactly. A provider or coordinator seeing a mismatch should treat the response as invalid rather than attempt best-effort parsing.

taskId.description: The upgrade_tasks.id this proposal is for.

runId.description: The upgrade_runs.id this response belongs to. Optional at response-authoring time — the coordinator may assign/stamp this after receiving the response.

provider.description: Which provider produced this response. Extend this enum, don't repurpose an existing value, when a new provider is added.

stage.description: proposal = first read-only pass. review = a second provider's independent review of a proposal or diff. implementation = the approved code-writing pass (only reachable after the implementation-approval gate).

understanding.description: The provider's restatement of the problem/request in its own words. Used to catch misunderstood requests before any code gets written.

rootCauseHypothesis.description: Optional. Only meaningful for bug-fix-shaped requests; omit for pure feature requests.

affectedFiles.description: Repo-relative paths. Implementation runs must not touch files outside this list without a revised proposal — an implementation diff touching an unlisted file is a review finding, not something to wave through.

risks.description: Correctness, performance, or UX risks. May be empty (validated as [] , not omitted) if the provider genuinely found none — omission is treated as "didn't check," not "none found."

privacyOrSecurityConcerns.description: Separate from general risks because these get surfaced more prominently in the review UI. Empty array, not omitted, if none apply.

testPlan.description: Concrete, checkable steps — not "add appropriate tests." At least one item required; a proposal with no test plan is incomplete.

expectedUserImpact.description: What the user will actually notice changes, in plain language — this is what gets shown in the approval UI, not the technical diff summary.

effort.description: Coarse sizing only. small = single file, no new deps. medium = a few files, possibly a new small dep. large = cross-cutting or touches sync/schema — should push the reviewer toward extra scrutiny.

blockers.description: Open questions or missing information the provider needs before it can proceed confidently. A non-empty blockers array on a proposal run should route to "needs clarification" rather than "ready for approval" in the client UI.
